notes: Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-d67081, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by session cc-442dc5 (review job issue #1070). I fetched arXiv 2103.09945v2 myself; its SHA-256 is 62d26eb931f271404c333c4b9a929e85239222788834cf16dcec1dff230c34c8, matching the recorded hash. Verdict: accept. All 14 sourceIssues are confirmed — I checked each at its locator, and settled E9 on the page image because pdftotext drops the prime that the finding is about. The strongest are E10 and E14, two distinct unjustified steps in the proof of Lemma 6.3.3 (p. 60) that both turn on the phrase 'any lift': eigenvalues of absolute value 1 give compactness only for a semisimple element, and an arbitrary real lift of the class in G/w(G_m) need not have the required quotient class. E2 is confirmed decisively — Definition 3.1.6 has only clauses (1) and (2), and (2) is the closed immersion of local models the text needs — and E5, E6, E7, E9 and E13 are each contradicted by the paper's own neighbouring sentences. E11 is a real gap in a citation's hypotheses: [Poo04, Corollary 3.4] is stated for a smooth quasi-projective subscheme of P^n, and it is applied to a smooth chart produced by [LMB00, Théorème 6.3], whose quasi-projectivity is not checked. No later version or erratum corrects any of them: arXiv stops at v2 and Crossref's record of the DOI carries no update; the final Annals text is paywalled and, as the extraction states, was not compared. Two classes of defect were repaired in place, both because sourceIssues feed the public errata register: (1) the run-together spacing throughout the source's venue and version fields and every finding's locator, printed text, correction and reason ('arXiv2103.09945v2, p9,§2.2.2', 'Definition3.1.6', 'Annals of Mathematics202(2025),no.3'); and (2) leaked process text — seven reasons carried the extraction's own session id and an internal revision note, '(cc-442dc5) Reclassified to affect nothing:', which is now removed with the substantive justification kept. Everything else holds: all 23 library items' declarations resolve at the pinned commits; the 25 planned items go to 25 distinct stages that each plan them (RG2.4's decompositions, BG0's torsors and isocrystals, BG1's Kottwitz and Newton invariants, R07.4's Breuil–Kisin modules, ShimuraData D3/D4); no missing item is in either library (Shimura varieties, local models, affine Grassmannians, Honda–Tate, Newton strata, Kottwitz maps and displays all return nothing); and the 162 missing items are routed exactly once across twelve routes, whose six Part II parents all exist, whose ids are all free, whose titles begin with their parents' and whose areas are all galaxy ids. Two observations for the maintainer, neither a defect: most locators are terse ('4.2.8', 'Proof of 5.2.3') and give no page, so verifying them means searching the PDF; and seven items are the extraction's own continuation lemmas rather than statements of the paper, with locators like 'Continuation: proof of Kisin–Zhou 5.2.3 or 5.2.7' — they are the repair steps for E11 and E12 (items C14–C24) and are useful, but a reader should know they are not in the paper. python3 scripts/check_paper.py reports ok.
